sources.note: The best hits per target less the penalties, divided by the stage time, give the hit factor; the best hit factor of the stage earns the stage's maximum points and the others get points in proportion.

sources.page: 9.4.1, p. 29 (PDF p. 35); Appendix B2 IPSC Target, p. 49 (PDF p. 55); Appendix C2 IPSC Poppers, p. 52 (PDF p. 58); Appendix C3 IPSC Metal Plates, p. 53 (PDF p. 59)
sources.note: Zone values of the paper target per power factor; a handgun hit on a scoring popper or plate is worth 5 points with either power factor. The IPSC Mini Target of Appendix B3 has the same values.

Each miss, each penalized no-shoot hit and each procedural penalty takes 10 points off; on one paper or metal no-shoot at most two hits are penalized. A disappearing target (9.9.2) incurs no miss penalty.
Production, Production Optics and Optics state no major rating. In Revolver, a revolver holding 7 or more rounds does not qualify for major (Appendix D5 item 15).

Appendix D1 item 8, p. 55 (PDF p. 61); D3 item 20, p. 57 (PDF p. 63); D4 item 18.2, p. 58 (PDF p. 64); D4a item 18.2, p. 60 (PDF p. 66); D6 item 8, p. 63 (PDF p. 69)
sources.note: Round limits count the rounds in a magazine at the start signal. Standard Division limits the handgun with its magazine by a gauge box (Appendix D2 item 15), not by a length or a count, so it has no entry; Revolver has no cylinder limit (D5 item 15).
Moving targets may be used, set off by IPSC targets or by mechanical or electrical devices; 9.9 says when a moving target counts as disappearing.
